hook: *74%* of Telangana citizens rely on their own two-wheeler
hook_b: *74%* of Telangana citizens rely on their own two-wheeler
tldr: Cyberabad Moves, a three-day summit on traffic and urban mobility, begins today with international experts, the DGP and CM Revanth Reddy.

beats.what: The summit runs panel discussions, two breakout sessions and an ideathon; the CM is to present the ideathon awards.
beats.why: Cyberabad and West Hyderabad face growing congestion, CMC Commissioner G. Srijana said.
beats.care: Talks are on with TGRTC over the bus shortage in the IT corridor and last-mile connectivity.

cards.title: 🆕 What's new
cards.body: CP M. Ramesh contrasted Telangana with London, where he said 97% of commuters use public transport and 9,000 buses carry more people than the Underground.

cards.q: What would get you out of your own vehicle in the IT corridor?

qs: Can 1,000 new buses a year keep pace with Cyberabad's growth?

facts.t: The summit drew *1,172* individual registrations plus 93 schools, 27 colleges and 62 RWAs.

viz.verdict: Figures cited by the Cyberabad CP to show the gap in public transport use.

watch: What the CM announces at the summit and the ideathon winners.

sources.name: The Hindu
sources.title: Cyberabad Moves summit to focus on traffic congestion, public transport and urban mobility

fact: *74%* of Telangana citizens depend on personal two-wheelers, says Cyberabad CP
twist: The state plans to add *1,000* buses a year for the next four to five years.
